post_title: I work in parking for PSU — please read this
post_body:
Hi everyone, I work in parking for PSU. Please read this to better understand parking on campus

Hi everyone, as the semester is about to start I thought it would be helpful to make this post and inform you guys on some advice on parking. I feel like this will help incoming students on how we approach parking and where you can park at a given time. It can be difficult at times, so I hope this alleviates any issues.
If a parking garage closes and you don't have a pass SPECIFICALLY for that garage, you will be turned away. For example, if you have an SCR or CR pass, that's good for the commuter lots only. I understand new passes this semester will have maps on them to show which lots the pass is good for. If you see one of us out there with a sign that says "Lot Full", that's when you won't be able to park if you lack a pass.
Because of the above point, I don't recommend trying to park in the Hub. It's too small for the amount of traffic it gets and you're likely going to be turned away to park downtown or in another garage. It fills up so quickly.
We do have to leave room for passholders when we close the garage, so asking if it's "actually full" or seeing there's open spots on the counter still isn't grounds to let you in. It is imperative for us that the spaces never go down to zero.
If the plate readers don't get your plate, scan your PSU ID, the parking pass is attached to that.
Sometimes the garages close for or get reserved for events, and you'll probably get turned away as a result.
For football weekends there is an event rate of about $40 to park. It's so busy that we even have to restrict passholders coming in; we typically let passholders in if they have to work that day, too, but not if they're going to the game. And again, if a garage closes and your pass isn't for there, you will be turned away.
I understand it can be frustrating when a garage closes, but don't argue with us, ignore and blow past us, or threaten to get us fired. Arguing is wasting both of our time, and it has the potential to cause a backup. We do file reports on particularly hostile or rude customers, and HR and Student Affairs do read these reports.
Ignoring and blowing past us when we redirect you will not only result in a report, but Parking Enforcement gets notified, too. Your ticket can also be deactivated, meaning you'll pay a lost ticket fee ($24) on top of the $50-$150 ticket you'll get (depending on the violation). It's not worth hurting your wallet for that.
For anyone in tour groups: please try to avoid parking in the Hub. Yes, it's where you meet at the end of it, but the capacity cannot hold the tour groups as well as passholders. There are instructions in both the email and links provided to park in the commuter lots and take the bus from there. It's also free if you park in the Commuter Lots and got the code in advance.
I can't believe I have to say this, but we do send out emails to passholders and do expect you to read them. They include instructions on there to help park or notify passholders of events that might disrupt your ability to park. Reading the emails saves you alot of effort in the long run, so please please read them. I apologize if this sounds patronizing, but we do see the emails and it gets very obvious when someone hasn't read it.
Hope this helps everyone!
Edit: one thing I forgot to mention, if you get too many tickets then your parking privileges get revoked. You can't park on campus whatsoever and your vehicle will be towed if it's found to be parked on campus. There's been at least one or two football players who incurred this.
Thanks! Very helpful. Another thing you might want to add is instructions on how to sign up for the PSU Parking listserv. That has been helpful to me.
I used to be hybrid, got a pass and had to walk from West Deck to my former place of employment. I never complained. Furthermore, Eisenhower Deck is listed up there, that's centrally located and you can get to most places pretty easily from there.
Not everyone in on core campus and the lots around my office building are empty. No worries, I just come in and spend most of the day walking back and forth to the pay by the hour lot every two hours to pump more quarters in. Very Productive.
West Deck MIGHT be opening up sales for more permits, I'm not sure. There's also a new Tempo parking that has a link on the transportation website; you can pay $4.50 to park at Eisenhower or another lot listed for the day, assuming there's room. That's been taking pressure off of the decks.
If you're not willing to do that, East, West, and usually Nittany are open, Hub I don't recommend still. Even with the tempo taking pressure off, I still close at 10:30 - 11:00 and 1:00 - 2:00 pretty consistently, and there's no telling when I'll open up. And if there's an event, then I'm going to be closed earlier and for longer. I'm at hub this month, I expect to be going to Nittany next month.
I've had the SCR parking pass for spring, summer, and fall semesters for the past 4 years. For those who dont know already, yes, you can park in parking garages and various lots around campus, it just has to be designated as an evening/weekend lot and you can only park there after 4pm on weekdays and any time on the weekend. The way to find these lots is by checking the psu interactive parking map.
I dont even work for parking but I had a student enter my building cursing me out because his car was towed.
The student parked in a clinic parking spot 15 minutes only and went to class. He came to my desk and demanded to know where his car was and why I had it towed. He also demanded I look at the cameras because he knows there are some around the buildings. Sir. Im and admin for a program and havent left my desk since 8am
I appreciate the effort to post this information.
Is there a guide for non-pass holders (eg parents visiting)?
Im always confused where I can and cant park when I go to visit as a parent, eg what garages allow and have space for visitors, and what the on street parking rules actually are. Seems like if you park incorrectly for more than 3 minutes, Walks is already hooking your car up to their truck.
Nice. I used Honk for the first time and got a ticket at a spikes game even though I paid in the correct zone.
Youre really swimming upstream trying to make the parking office seem competent.
The transportation services parking site is confusing. How do I find my parking chair, I'd like to purchase a parking pass for the fall in West deck
This needs to be told to everyone. I absolutely despise working at the Hub since it always fills up and last month was the first time that I didn't have one incident there. The clientele is some of the most entitled at PSU, and I am dreading the start of the semester because of the amount of hostility and entitlement I get.
I had one student at East Deck ignore me and then ripped up his ticket in front of me and then tried to justify him entering by saying "I have class!" I hear that excuse a million times a day, that's never a valid reason to make an exception.
Had another student at Hub Deck say he was going to count the spaces and would report me if there was room. He then started taking photos of me and said he'd call the cops to get me fired.     Student Affairs was really pissed that I had to deal with that.
And both students were driving BMWs, I wonder what the common thread is. I'm really tempted to share the Hub guy's plate since it was a dealer car (so not his), but it isn't worth my job.
Yep, these are classic signs of entitled kids. They have wealthy parents who buy influence at their country clubs and social circles, so they pass on these traits to their kiddies. The rules are for the dummies who are ignorant enough to think they can't be bent or broken. They're just a little more special than us common folk.
I am currently building an app for college parking app. It shows real time per parking spot availability.
Our app helps you park faster. The app shows a live map of all the lots on a college campus and marks which spaces are free right now. You open it before you arrive, see an open spot, and drive straight there. It updates every few seconds, so the info stays fresh. We dont track who you areonly whether a space is empty or taken.
Do you think this would be beneficial to you guys? looking for honest feedback.
Man Ive gotten a parking ticket in Lion Heart gym parking lot(I lived above it) on a damn Sunday night (gym closed) unloading groceries with my flashers on. I couldnt give a flying fuck what you have to say in this post lol. I saw the person writing the ticket and tried to explain this, they dont care. Same energy as a damn hall monitor in elementary school
What makes you think I get paid for the amount of people who go into the garage or there's a set quota? There is a general number I have to keep in mind and restrict entry if it gets to it, but I get zero bonus for letting people in or out.
Furthermore I have to take the job fairly seriously since folks pay $45 a month for these passes. If a garage fills up and pass holders can't get in - which has happened - that's a problem. Idk why you seem to think I have a financial incentive to turn people away, I have a job and I'm going to do it.
Exactly, thank you! The comment above shows you the type of BS I have to deal with on a regular basis. I'm trying to get a new job since quite frankly I didn't earn a master's degree to work in a parking garage. I wouldn't mind the job so much if it weren't for the constant disrespect and the low pay.
